identificationModule.briefTitle: A Rollover Study of Ixabepilone (BMS-247550) In Patients With Metastatic Breast Cancer Previously Treated With An Anthracycline
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Rollover Study of Ixabepilone (BMS-247550) In Patients With Metastatic Breast Cancer Previously Treated With An Anthracycline And Who Are Taxane Resistant Who Have Completed Study CA163107 And Who Are Benefiting From Continuation On Therapy With Ixabepilone

descriptionModule.briefSummary: To provide extended access to Ixabepilone therapy to subjects with metastatic breast cancer who have completed the previous Phase II study (CA163-107)

primaryOutcomes.measure: Provide extended access to Ixabepilone therapy to subjects with metastatic breast cancer who have completed the previous Phase II study (CA163107) and are benefiting from continuation on therapy with Ixabepilone as determined by the treating investigator
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: 21-day cycles until documented disease progression or unacceptable toxicity

primaryOutcomes.measure: To evaluate the frequency and the severity of observed adverse reactions in treated patients, graded according to the NCI Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Version 3.0
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: 21-day cycles until documented disease progression or unacceptable toxicity

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Secondary objectives will be assessed by combining data with the previous Phase II study CA163107
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: 21-day cycles until documented disease progression or unacceptable toxicity

secondaryOutcomes.measure: To evaluate the antitumor response according to the RECIST criteria
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: 21-day cycles until documented disease progression or unacceptable toxicity

secondaryOutcomes.measure: To evaluate the duration of achieved responses

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Women aged 20 years or older
* Patients with metastatic breast cancer whose primary lesion was definitely diagnosed to be breast by histological or cellular examination

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status (PS) of ≥2
